messages:
Isabel (support): Hey team — escalated from AcmeCorp. They report streaming responses (SSE) cut off ~18-25s into stream. Client logs show ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING and browser reconnect loop. Billing spike noted: two partial requests billed as full.

Ryan (eng): Can you paste a minimal reproducer and any request/response headers? Cloudflare in front? Which LB (ALB/NLB/nginx) in front of our origin?

Isabel (support): Repro provided by customer (reduced):
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?prompt=test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST --data-binary '{"model":"gpt-small"}'
```
Symptoms: stream starts, first few "data: {...}" chunks arrive, then a 0-length chunk, then connection closes. Browser shows: "ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING". They also see a small HTML snippet appended in the last bytes ("<html>...challenge...</html>"). Cloudflare in front (proxed), origin behind ALB -> nginx -> app.

Olivia (infra): HTML snippet suggests Cloudflare Access/Challenge or Worker/Page rules injecting content on 4xx/5xx. Also check Cloudflare "Auto Minify" and "Brotli" — those can force buffering. On ALB side default idle timeout is 60s; if client expects longer keepalive, mismatch can cause half-close. Two-pronged hypothesis: origin or auth layer returns a short HTML error mid-stream (401/403) during token rotation or rate-limit; Cloudflare then transforms response (minify/HTML injection) and sends buffered close -> client sees corrupted chunk stream.

Emma (support): Customer also pasted client trace:
```
[stream] data chunk ok
[stream] data chunk ok
[stream] connection closed unexpectedly
[http] 0 bytes received
[error] ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING
[reconnect] new request -> 401 (token refresh) -> full JSON error body
```
They said token rotation happens around 25s for their integration (short-lived token). Could be auth refresh race.

Ryan (eng): Actionable checks:
- Capture full tcpdump between CF and ALB to confirm who injected HTML.
- Check nginx logs for "upstream prematurely closed connection" or "client aborted".
- Confirm our streaming handler never emits an HTML body for 4xx/5xx mid-stream (should stream an event with error meta instead).
- Repro with curl passing `--raw` and `--no-buffer` flags; try bypassing CF (direct to ALB) to isolate.

Isabel (support): Customer added quick bypass test (direct to ALB): same stream continues longer but still cuts at ~25s, last bytes are a tiny HTML fragment: `<!doctype html><html><body>Challenge</body></html>`. They also shared nginx error: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`.

Olivia (infra): Immediate mitigations to propose to customer: 
- Disable Cloudflare Auto Minify/Brotli for the streaming path or create a page rule to bypass performance features for `*/v1/stream*`.
- Set response header `Cache-Control: no-transform` from origin to prevent CF from changing body.
- Set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) and `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection "";` to avoid buffering within nginx.
- Increase ALB idle timeout to 300s to avoid close races.

Ryan (eng): Longer-term fixes on our side: 
- Make streaming endpoints tolerant to mid-stream auth refresh: avoid returning HTML error bodies mid-stream; instead send a JSON SSE error event or a proper chunked error that clients can handle.
- Add instrumentation to track mid-stream status code changes and correlate with token rotation events.
- Add a short-lived header `X-Stream-Start: <ts>` so proxies won't coalesce based on heuristics.

Emma (support): I'll send customer the workaround steps (disable CF minify, add no-transform header, nginx buffering off, ALB timeout bump) and collect tcpdump/nginx logs. Also opening billing ticket for the duplicate charges while we investigate.

SupportBot: Ticket created: #INC-2024-7723 (assigned to eng-infra).

Olivia (infra): If you need a quick reproducer for infra to test, run:
```bash
# server: simulate streaming that flips to 401 mid-stream
python3 - <<'PY'
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
import time
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
  def do_POST(self):
    self.send_response(200)
    self.send_header('Content-Type','text/event-stream')
    self.send_header('Transfer-Encoding','chunked')
    self.send_header('Cache-Control','no-transform')
    self.end_headers()
    self.wfile.write(b'6\r\ndata: {"part":1}\r\n\r\n')
    self.wfile.flush()
    time.sleep(20)
    # simulate auth flip - send HTML error mid-stream
    self.wfile.write(b'1a\r\n<html>Auth</html>\r\n\r\n')
PY
```
This reproduces the client-side chunk parse error when proxies buffer/transform.

Emma (support): Thanks — marking as P1 for customer impact. Assigning eng-infra + eng-runtime to investigate. Will update customer with the workaround and request direct logs. :thumbsup:
